newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-CAPRIATI AND MAJOLI BOW OUT OF AUSTRALIAN OPEN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-CAPRIATI AND MAJOLI BOW OUT OF AUSTRALIAN OPEN.

text.p: World number one Pete Sampras and Swiss teenager Martina Hingis marched into the second round of the Australian Open on Tuesday but former prodigy Jennifer Capriati broke down in tears after an unexpected defeat.
Sampras, top seed and favourite for the men's title, crushed Romanian qualifier Dinu Pescariu 6-2 6-4 6-2.
The 16-year-old Hingis picked up a warning for racket abuse before beating German veteran Barbara Rittner 6-1 7-5 on Centre Court.
Sixth seeded Croat Iva Majoli lost 7-5 6-1 to unheralded Patty Schnyder of Switzerland in the biggest upset on a day when the top players dominated.

The greatest drama came off court in the media room where Capriati, whom Hingis replaced as the sport's teenaged darling, burst into tears after being ousted in the first round of her Australian Open comeback.

Four years after her last appearance in Melbourne, when she reached the quarter-finals at the age of 16, Capriati was beaten 6-2 3-6 6-4 by fellow American Jolene Watanabe in a performance which left a crowd of fans disappointed.
After reaching the final of a Sydney warm-up tournament on Saturday, Capriati had been expected to enjoy a straightforward passage into the second round.
But Watanabe, a 28-year-old who had never before advanced beyond the first round of the Australian Grand Slam event, was able to stay on the baseline and watch Capriati throw the match away.
"I was pretty disappointed. I didn't think I was playing nearly as well as last week," Capriati told a news conference.

Asked how she felt about the warm public support she has enjoyed since returning to tennis, Capriati started to reply: "Just being out there and hearing the crowd..." but then burst into tears and was escorted away sobbing heavily.
Czechoslovak-born Hingis was warned by the umpire for throwing her racket into the net after a service break against her in the second set led to a string of errors.
Even if Hingis fails to deny top seed Steffi Graf a fifth Australian Open crown, her financial future is secure.
An Italian sportswear firm on Tuesday announced a five-year sponsorship deal which will give Hingis at least $7.5 million and up to $12 million if she ousts Graf from the top spot.
Men's 11th seed and former champion Jim Courier survived a first-round scare against Dutchman Sjeng Schalken, beating him 8-6 in the fifth set of a marathon tussle.
Like Sampras and German Boris Becker before him, Courier complained that the balls being used in the tournament were too soft.
But tournament director Paul McNamee said the balls were no different from those used last year.
On a sweltering but blustery second day, third seeded Croat Goran Ivanisevic mastered the awkward conditions, hammering 15 aces to demolish Australian qualifier Ben Ellwood in straight sets.

Women's second seed Arantxa Sanchez Vicario and men's 10th seed Albert Costa added to Spain's early successes with straight-sets victories. All five Spanish seeds in the tournament have advanced to the second round.
Dutchman Jan Siemerink, seeded 13, was the only top man to fall on Tuesday, losing in five sets to Norway's Christian Ruud.
